summary: King County, WA lookout: an L-4 cab from Galena Mountain (1941), an AWS cabin (1942) and a second L-4 cab (1953); removed or destroyed in 1969, with foundations reported on site.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1941), AWS cabin (1942), L-4 cab again (1953)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1969; a WillhiteWeb visit (undated in the source) found the rocky perch and foundations still on the site

access.note: Drive-up gravel road with a winter gate closure; the summit area has communication towers and fencing

visit.trail_note: No cab stands on the site, so there is nothing to climb. The summit is a communications area with fencing; check any posted rules before going.

resolved_conflicts.field: arrival of the Galena cab on Maloney Ridge
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Galena Mountain page, Forest Lookouts and Firelookout.com date the move to 1941, and the register dates an L-4 cab to 1941. WillhiteWeb gives 1950. The record uses 1941, the date most sources give.
Register says removed in 1969; Forest Lookouts says removed by burning; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year matches, so the record uses removed.

notes_for_editor: The 1941 versus 1950 date for the Galena cab is the main dispute; the story gives both. The Forest Lookouts index lists the entry under Snoqualmie National Forest, a header that is not treated as an agency conflict. The register coordinates (47.69518, -121.33798) were not checked against WillhiteWeb, which places the lookout nearer Sobieski Mountain; check before publishing a map pin. WillhiteWeb's visit describes a trail beside a fenced communications area; the story gives no directions to the foundations, and the record's visit note asks for posted rules to be checked. The 1941 date also appears in a search snippet from Summitpost, which was not read and is not cited.
